evidence: Each deposition cycle consisted of a titanium precursor pulse, a N2 purge, followed by an oxygen precursor pulse and another purge. The pulse and purge sequence was 0.75 s/0.5 s/0.5 s/0.5 s for the TTIP–H2O precursor system, and 0.4 s/0.5 s/0.5 s/0.5 s for the TiCl4–H2O system. Most films were deposited on n-type Si 〈100〉 wafers (Virginia Semiconductor Inc., Fredericksburg, VA), but polycarbonate substrates (Lexan, GE Plastics, Pittsfield, MA) were also used. Both types of substrates were cleaned by water plasma prior to film deposition, which was shown to increase the concentration of surface hydroxyl groups. 11,12 All the single-layer titania films were deposited at 80 °C, and the number of deposition cycles was either 1400 (using TiCl4–H2O) or 1000 (using TTIP–H2O) to give a film thickness around 100 nm.
